answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 56% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. Because the ferrous forfeiture is applied at exit, the ledge ledger totals each burn, and the knoll audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 73 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 25 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
